changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `54a78308a` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1837 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2449 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36774994970)

| Metric | Value | Budget |
|--------|-------|--------|
| **Eager closure** (gzip, 330 chunks) | **3582.7 KB** | 3607.4 KB |
| Main entry chunk (gzip) | 149.9 KB | 350 KB |
| Entry file | `index-DqJVK6Rr.js` | — |
| Status | **PASS** | — |

The **eager closure** is every chunk the entry reaches through static imports — what the browser fetches and parses before the app renders. The entry chunk on its own is a small fraction of it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3cd7a994d11f9f6dff67a5e10b130a87e51a5841`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #11232 (body; triage `5915804318`; serial note `5916014553`; claim `5918635427`; dev report `5919488482`), PR #11265 (body, its 3 files, the net diff against `main` from the branch point `02a22957c0`: +633/−7), and the head's check-runs, read twice. Read-only beside them: #11203, #11204 with PR #11230, #11189. Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Accept sets and public surface: none move.** `useDraftAutoSave` and `DraftSend` are module-private to `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`; its only readers are the four in-file callers. `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` exports `StudioDesignSurface` and `StudioDesignSurfaceProps` from that file, not the pillars and not the hook. The new `target: string` option is required, so a caller that omits it is a type error, and `Type Check` is green on the head: all four pass it. `StudioDesignSurfaceProps` is unchanged. Named right.

**(a) The binding, read at source.** `pendingRef` now carries `target` and `since`; the layout effect keeps `since` while the dirty flag stays up (`dirty && prev.dirty ? prev.since : target`) and takes the current target otherwise. The timer and `flush` refuse a period whose `since` differs from `target`; a claim's `unmoved()` also requires `target === sentFor`. Per caller, for the card's letter (one switch inside the debounce, the new load slow):
- Automations (`flow:NAME`): `setCurrent` changes the target in the same commit, `autoDirty` falls only in the load's `finally`, and the timer's deps (`dirty`, `blocked`, `snapKey`) do not change on the switch, so the running timer fires and is refused by `owned()`; the `finally` ends the period. A fast load clears the flag first and the effect clears the timer. Sound.
- Interfaces page inspector (`leafKey`): the same shape; `setIfDirty(false)` after the load's await ends the period. Sound.
- Data (`object:NAME`): the load effect clears `dirty` synchronously; the one commit between `setCurrent` and that clear reads `since ≠ target` and is refused too. The control holds by two mechanisms now, and its switch is untouched (d). Sound.
- Interfaces nav (`app:NAME`): with the pillar keyed by package (c) the hook instance is fresh on a package switch, and in-package `appName` does not change, so `since === target` throughout: the nav autosave, `flush` (#11189's Done) and the claim behave as PR #11230 left them. Sound.
- In flight, all four: every post-await clear goes through `sent.unmoved()` (page `:2239`, nav `:2285`, Data `:3443` and `doReorderFields` `:3492`, Automations `:4367`), and the claim is taken with the target of the commit that sent it, so a save of the previous item that lands after the switch never clears the flag of the item opened since. Pinned on the page inspector (leg C: exactly 1 red); the mechanism is one `claim`, so one pin carries it. Sound.

⛔ "Never write the old buffer to the new target" holds on every path the card's letter names: the pending send is refused, and an in-flight send addressed its own item when it was taken (`doSave` captured `current`). It is a binding by item identity, not by buffer provenance, and the period ends only when the caller drops its flag; that leaves one blind spot outside the letter, under ③.

**(b) Drop, not re-target.** Triage's letter is "cancels or re-targets", and it names `DataPillar`'s synchronous clear (a drop) as the fallback shape, so a drop is inside it. It is stated in the PR (its own section, four reasons), in the changeset and in the hook's comment, and it is pinned: the three leaf pins assert `server.saves` empty after the switch and again after the load, so the old item receives nothing either. It is what `main` already does whenever the load lands inside the debounce (the page inspector's `setIfDirty(false)`, Automations' `finally`, Data's synchronous clear); the fix makes the slow-load path agree with the fast one. Not a regression of #11204: with no switch the claim's target comparison is a no-op, and PR #11230's letter (an edit during an in-flight save of the same item lands in the next save) is untouched. The one edit this PR drops that #11230 would have sent is one typed on the previous item's buffer while it is shown under the next item, which could only have landed on the wrong page. Right.

**(c) The package-switch member.** `StudioDesignSurface` renders `InterfacesPillar` with `key={packageId}` at its mount site. Inside the claim's conditional surface: the claim names "`InterfacesPillar`'s `PackageSwitcher`: only if the hook fix does not cover them", and triage's preferred shape for #11203 is verbatim "keying `InterfacesPillar` by package", which only its mount site can do. That the hook does not cover it is true at source: the app-load effect's `!isSameApp` branch installs the next package's app and clears neither `navDirty` nor `editNav`, so with the hook alone the flag never falls and every send on the next package would be refused for good. The console route (the `:packageId/:tab` element in `StudioRoute.tsx`) keeps the surface mounted across a package switch, as the harness does, so the key is live in production. #11203's three pins are present and read right: a confirmed discard sends 0 app saves after 3.5 s with editing closed and nothing held; an edit after the switch saves `beta_app` in `com.beta.app`; a cancelled discard keeps Acme and its item, which then saves to `acme_app` in `com.acme.app`. Beside them the slow-app-load variant and the page inspector on a package switch, which #11203's triage asked measured in the same pass. The pillar's unmount cleanups report `false` and `null` to the surface, so the leave guard and the dock label release with the remount. Right.

**(d) `DataPillar`.** One required option and one comment on its hook call; its list effect, load effect, switch and both saves are the base's. Inside ⛔ "not `DataPillar`'s switch". Right.

**Pins against the ruling's list.** Automations and the page inspector reproduce first (4 of 6 red at the branch point; 6 of 8 red on the base leg); Data is the control; a switch inside the debounce sends 0 saves to the newly opened item on each; an edit after the load saves normally on each. All present. Ablation A (the timer's `owned()` a no-op) 3 red, C (the claim's target comparison removed) 1 red, each as predicted; B under ③.

**Check-runs on the head** (conclusions are the gate verdicts): 35 success, 3 skipped (the two coverage rows and dependabot). On the second read `Test (shard 2/8)`, `Test (shard 4/8)`, `Test (shard 6/8)` and `Test (shard 7/8)` are still `in_progress`: not concluded, read as neither pass nor fail. `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Build & E2E`, `Test (dist pins)`, shards 1, 3, 5 and 8, the five changeset gates and the rest: success. `main` moved three commits past the branch point; none touches `studio-design/` (changesets only), and the PR reads mergeable.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11232-autosave-send-bound-to-target.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. Right: a behaviour fix inside the Studio surface; no export, prop, type, schema or accepted set moves. The hook and the pillars are not on the package index, and the remount on a package switch is behaviour of the exported `StudioDesignSurface`, not its API. The changeset's text matches the diff: the four callers named, the drop named, the package key named. `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`: success. `Clause-②: no` on the PR and the claim: right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
1. `DataPillar` gains `target`: inside the ⛔ (d).
2. The key at the mount site, not inside the pillar: inside the conditional surface, and triage's preferred shape (c).
3. Pins beyond the list (the page inspector on a package switch; a save in flight across a page switch): the first #11203's triage asked for, the second is the ruling's "in-flight send" clause. Right to add.
4. The base leg by a whole-file swap: a measurement note, no bearing on the diff.
5. Leg B, predicted 2 red, observed 3 (f). Consistent with the diff: `doNavSave`'s deps are `[client, appName, appDraft, onDraftSaved]`, without `packageId`, so with the key deleted and the next package's app name not yet committed (the `act()` hold), the timer read `since === target === app:acme_app` and sent the discarded edit to `acme_app` in `com.acme.app`: the old buffer to its old target, not a cross-write, but against the author's confirmed discard. The same interleaving is real when the next package's app list is slow. So the key holds that pin for the reason the PR states, and the extra red sharpens rather than hides the PR's "which covers which": the hook never covers a package switch. No pin passes for a wrong reason.
6. Build closure at `e4594fdc66` with the source identical: accepted; `Build & E2E` is green on the head regardless.
7. Probes never committed: the file list is the three files.
8. No merge of `main`: checked, nothing on this surface to merge.

`open_questions`: none.

The PR's acceptance notes and the report's `out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:
- **A page-inspector edit dropped on a package switch** (report entry 3; PR note 1). Accepted under the discard rule and stated. The leave guard mirrors `navDirty` only, so a page edit under 1.5 s old is dropped by the remount without a prompt; before, it reached its own page by a stale closure (`doSave` has no `packageId` in its deps), and every later edit on that still-open page went to the wrong package, which is the defect fixed. Not #11204's letter (no save in flight). The pillar-tab switch drops the same edit today. Fileable, low: the surface's leave guard holds nav edits only, and a page-inspector edit is not held on a package switch.
- **An in-flight save's UI effects** (`setHasDraft`, `setError`) land on the item opened since: no write, read at source. A note for the family card below.
- **Finding 1, the load window** (three pillars: the previous item's buffer shown and editable under the new item until its load lands; the autosave, the enable toggle and add-field write it into the new item). Outside this card's letter: the dirty period begins after the switch, so it is not a switch inside the debounce, and the enable toggle is an explicit save outside the hook. Same family: the buffer saved is not the target's. Pre-existing, read at source on the base, which has no binding at all. For the seat to file.
- **Finding 2, Automations on a package switch** (package A's open flow stays open on B, and an edit saves it with B's `packageId`; Data read the same). Outside this card's letter: triage's family enumeration names the nav autosave as the package-switch member, and the claim keys nothing but `InterfacesPillar`. It is #11203's exact shape on the two unkeyed pillars, and a one-line key at the same mount site closes it, but the `DataPillar` slot is under this order's ⛔, so the stop is right. For the seat to file.
- **One more from this review, same family.** The page inspector's load effect has a branch that replaces the buffer without ending the period: `if (!current || !isEditable) { setDraft({}); setHasDraft(false); return; }` clears no `ifDirty`. Edit a page, open an `object` leaf (a studio-canvas leaf: `isEditable` false, `blocked` true, so nothing is sent there), then reopen the same page: `since` and `target` are both that page again, the buffer is `{}`, and if the page's reload takes over 1.5 s the timer sends `{}` as that page's draft. Pre-existing on `main` (the base has no `owned()` and sends it the same way); outside the letter (the write goes to the item the edit began on, so the ⛔ is not breached); read at source, not measured, and whether the server refuses an empty page body decides its weight. The hook's comment says "each caller's load clears it as it installs the new buffer", which this branch does not, so the comment overstates the caller contract by one branch.
